extracted.intended_audience: educational institutions (K-12 and postsecondary) and Title IX practitioners (Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, administrators, and legal counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for determining when sex-based conduct constitutes a hostile environment under Title IX, including definitions, required evidentiary perspectives, factors to consider, and procedural safeguards for recipients of Federal financial assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in these final regulations requires a recipient to restrict any rights protected by the First Amendment; the First Amendment may affect how a recipient responds to discriminatory harassment in the form of speech, and agencies are not stripped of power merely because regulations intersect with the First Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reiterates that final regs are intended to be consistent with case law regarding harassment and the First Amendment; recipients remain free to determine whether discipline is appropriate and what form it should take; private recipients are not compelled to abide by the Constitution and the Department will not require non-State actors to comply with the U.S. Constitution. Consider First Amendment and academic freedom when speech/expression issues are involved. See discussion at §106.6(d) and First Amendment section of the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of 'offensive' in subjective and objective standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'sex-based harassment' is revised to add the word 'offensive' to both the subjective and objective components of the hostile environment standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change addresses concerns about informal resolution of minor misconduct and confirms offensiveness is key to both perspectives. The Department emphasizes that both subjective and objective elements remain distinct and must each be supported by sufficient evidence; subjective offensiveness alone will not support a finding or discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severe or pervasive standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Hostile environment sex-based harassment is evaluated under a 'severe or pervasive' standard, consistent with Title VII and OCR's longstanding interpretation of Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct meets the 'severe or pervasive' standard if it limits or denies a person's ability to participate in or benefit from the recipient's education program or activity. The standard allows addressing conduct that is severe but not pervasive or pervasive but not severe. One stray remark generally will not satisfy pervasiveness; examples like graffiti, harassment in hallways, or persistent conduct that prevents completion of coursework could be pervasive. Recipients may consult Title VII law for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link to access: use of 'so' rather than 'sufficiently'
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation language is revised so that conduct must be 'so' severe or pervasive that it limits or denies participation or benefit from the education program or activity, replacing 'sufficiently.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This wording emphasizes that the severity/pervasiveness inquiry is necessarily linked to the complainant's access to education programs or activities. See §106.45 and §106.46 for evidence-gathering and evaluation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients are not required to affirmatively track speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the definition of 'sex-based harassment' or in §§106.44–106.46 requires a recipient to directly or indirectly track speech for which no complaint has been made or which the Title IX Coordinator has not been notified of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pervasiveness may be shown by widespread, openly practiced, or well-known conduct (e.g., graffiti, hallway harassment, recess incidents). Recipients should assess complaints/notifications considering the totality of known circumstances, including other related complaints. Recordkeeping obligations for speech-based complaints are treated the same as other complaints under §106.8(f)(1) and (2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual subjective and objective evaluation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Unwelcome sex-based conduct must be evaluated both subjectively (from the complainant's perspective) and objectively (from the perspective of a reasonable person in the complainant's position).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both elements are distinct and a decisionmaker must find sufficient evidence to satisfy each before concluding harassment occurred. Objective offensiveness is judged by a reasonable person standard; subjective offensiveness may be shown by the complainant's statements or other sources. Subjective offensiveness must be supported by evidence and by itself is insufficient to support a finding or discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality training and bias safeguards for personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators, investigators, and decisionmakers must be trained on how to serve impartially (including avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias) and to act without bias toward any specific party or complainants/respondents generally (§106.8(d)(2); §106.45(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must provide impartiality training; postsecondary cases must offer appeals on the basis that personnel had a conflict of interest or bias that would change the outcome (§106.46(i)(1)(iii)). Recipients' grievance procedure requirements (§106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46) are intended to protect due process and equitable treatment. Complainants or respondents who believe obligations were violated may file with OCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Limits or denies' access standard and impact evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex-based conduct is actionable if it 'limits or denies' a person's ability to participate in or benefit from the recipient's education program or activity; evidence of impact is required but no specific harm (e.g., lower grades) is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'limits' was placed first by the Department for clarity; 'limits' does not require proof of a particular harm. Evaluations must be fact-based and consider all relevant, non-impermissible evidence. Animus is not a required element; focus is on whether the conduct limits or denies participation based on sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to be considered in determining hostile environment
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-exhaustive list of factors informs whether conduct creates a hostile environment: the degree to which the conduct affected one or more students' education; the type, frequency, and duration of the conduct; the identity of and relationship between alleged harasser and subject(s); the number of individuals involved; the age and sex of the alleged harasser and subject(s); the size of the school, location of incidents, and context; other incidents at the school; incidents of gender-based but nonsexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors reflect a totality-of-the-circumstances approach similar to Title VII analyses. They are illustrative, not exhaustive, and recipients should consider the 'constellation of surrounding circumstances, expectations, and relationships.' Differences between employment and education contexts exist, but Title VII interpretations can inform Title IX evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples are illustrative; determinations require fact-specific totality analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Any examples provided (including in the NPRM or preamble) are illustrative only; a fuller, fact-specific analysis of the totality of circumstances is required to reach a final determination about hostile-environment sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to opine on specific examples in comments because each evaluation depends on the totality of circumstances; the administrative enforcement standard need not be identical to the damages standard in Davis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping parity for speech-based complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's recordkeeping obligations for complaints and notifications alleging verbal sex-based harassment should be treated the same as other complaints and notifications of sex discrimination (§106.8(f)(1) and (2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must maintain records for complaints/notifications consistent with the cited recordkeeping provisions; this does not imply an obligation to track unreported speech but requires treating reported speech-based incidents like other complaints for recordkeeping purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjective perspective is the complainant's
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation's reference to a subjective perspective refers to the complainant; evidence of the subjective element could include the complainant's own statements or other sources establishing the complainant's experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with Title VII precedent (Harris) and underscores that subjective perception is a required element but must be evaluated alongside the objective element.
